 Judgment

Since these two appeals arise from the very same award dated 06.11.2014 in O.P.(MV) No.344 of 2008 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, N. Paravur, these appeals are heard together and being disposed of by this judgment.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
M.A.C.A. No.653 of 2015 is filed by the 3rd respondent/insurer in the original petition, whereas M.A.C.A. No.224 of 2016 is filed by the claimants 1 to 3 in the OP.
2.

According to the claimants, on 12.04.2008 at about 8.30 p.m., while the victim sabu was travelling as a pillion rider of a motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KL-50/4582 ridden by his friend, a car bearing Reg. No.KL-10/AA-7007 driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner, hit on the motorcycle and as a result of the accident, the victim sabu sustained serious injuries and he succumbed to those injuries on 13.04.2008.

The claimants/ the wife, minor children and parents of the victim approached the tribunal claiming compensation under Section 166 of the Motor MACA Smt.Mini vs Smt. Nafeesa on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73784069/
3 Nos. 224 of 2016 & 653 of 2015 2026:KER:30608 Vehicles Act.
3. During the pendency of the original petition, claimants 4 and 5 namely the parents of the deceased died.

entities.text: Motor MACA Smt.Mini vs Smt. Nafeesa
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. Before the tribunal, the respondents 1 and 2, who are the registered owner and driver of the offending vehicle respectively, remained absent and they were set ex parte.
5. The 3rd respondent insurer filed written statement, admitting valid insurance policy but disputing the quantum of compensation claimed and denying negligence on the part of the car driver.
It was further contended that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle.
6. Before the tribunal, PW1 and PW2 were examined and Exts.A1 to A7 were marked.

The tribunal,
after analysing the evidence and materials on record, awarded a total sum of 24,12,000/- as compensation under different heads with interest @8% per annum with proportionate cost from the date of petition till realization.

7. Heard the learned Counsel for the claimants and MACA Nos. 224 of 2016 & 653 of 2015 2026:KER:30608 the learned Standing Counsel for the insurance company.
8.

The insurance company has preferred the M.A.C.A No.653 of 2015 contending that the amount awarded by the tribunal is exorbitant; that the monthly income of the deceased taken by the tribunal for assessing the compensation is on a higher side and therefore, the amount awarded as compensation is excessive.
Further, it was contended that the tribunal was not justified in taking 50% future prospects for the deceased as he was not having a permanent occupation or steady income.
It was also contended that the deceased had only three dependents and therefore the tribunal went wrong in deducting 1/4 th towards personal expenses.
9. Per contra, the learned counsel for the claimants contended that the victim was the bread winner of the family consisting of his wife, minor children and parents.
10. The accident is admitted by the insurance company.

The evidence on record would show that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of MACA Nos. 224 of 2016 & 653 of 2015 2026:KER:30608 the car bearing Reg. No.KL-10/AA-7007 driven by the 2 nd respondent which was insured with the 3rd respondent.

11. The specific case of the 1 st claimant, who is the widow of the deceased Sabu, is that her husband was toddy tapper and he was employed by the Toddy Tappers Co- operative Society at Quilandy in Kozhikode.

entities.text: Toddy Tappers Co- operative Society at Quilandy
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In support of the said case, claimants have produced Ext.A7 certificate and examined PW1, the Secretary of the Quilandy Toddy Tappers Co-operative Society, who issued Ext.A7.
In Ext.A7 it has been certified that the deceased sabu was drawing a monthly income of 10,800/-.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of PW1 and PW2 and Ext.A7 certificate.
Thus the learned tribunal was right in taking the monthly income of the deceased as 10,800/-.

Since the deceased Smt.Mini vs Smt. Nafeesa on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73784069/
4 was employed by the Toddy Tappers Co-operative Society at Quilandy, it cannot be termed as a temporary employment as contended by the 3rd respondent/ insurance company.

entities.text: Toddy Tappers Co-operative Society at Quilandy
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
12. Since the victim was aged 37 years at the time of accident, and he was a permanent employee,
50% of his MACA Nos. 224 of 2016 & 653 of 2015 2026:KER:30608 income is to be added towards the monthly income [ National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi [2017 (4) KLT 662 (SC)].

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi [2017 (4) KLT 662 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As on the date of accident and date of claim petition, respondents 4 and 5 in the original petition were alive and they were the dependents of the deceased.
Hence, the deceased had 5 dependents and 1/4 th of his income is to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
Then his monthly income would come to 16,200/- (10,800 + 5,400) and the multiplier to be adopted is "15".

Hence,
following the apex court judgments in Pranay Sethi (cited supra) and Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation [2010(2) KLT 802], the total compensation payable under the afore head is 2,187,000/- (12,150 x 12 x 15) as rightly calculated by the learned Tribunal.

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation [2010(2) KLT 802]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. Under the head loss of consortium, the learned Tribunal has awarded an amount of 1,00,000/-.

In the light of the Pranay Sethi (cited supra) claimants 1 to 5 are entitled to consortium of 40,000/-
with 10% increase in every 3 years.
The accident was on 13.04.2008, the award of MACA Nos. 224 of 2016 & 653 of 2015 2026:KER:30608 the Tribunal was on 06.11.2014.
Claimant No.1, who is the wife of the deceased is entitled to spousal consortium.
Claimant Nos. 2 and 3 the children of the deceased are entitled for parental consortium.
Claimant Nos. 4 and 5, the parents of the deceased are entitled for filial consortium.
Therefore, claimants are entitled to get 48,400/- each towards consortium (48,400 x 5 = 242000).

14. In New India Assurance Company v. Somwati and others [2020 KHC 6530], it has been held by the Apex Court that once compensation is awarded under the head loss of consortium, no amount shall be awarded under the head loss of love and affection, as it would amount to duplication of compensation.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company v. Somwati and others [2020 KHC 6530]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, claimants are not entitled to get any amount under the head loss of love and affection.
15. Under the head funeral expenses, the Tribunal has awarded an amount of 25,000/-.

In view of the guidelines of the Apex Court in Pranay Sethi's case (cited supra) claimants are entitled to only 15,000/- under the said head with 10% MACA Nos. 224 of 2016 & 653 of 2015 2026:KER:30608 interest every 3 year.
Hence, an amount of 18,150/- is to be awarded under the said head against 25,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
16. Going by the judgment in Pranay Sethi (cited supra), the compensation under the conventional head loss of estate ought to have been fixed at 15,000/- with 10% increase in every 3 years.

Thus,
following the judgment in Pranay Sethi (supra), the claimants are entitled to get 18,150/- towards loss of estate.
17. In the result, MACA No.224 of 2016 is allowed in part.
No cost.
MACA No.653 of 2015 is dismissed.
No cost.

The 3rd respondent is liable to pay the award amount as enhanced by this Court with 8% interest per annum from the date of petition till realisation.
